beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. Bao Xing's animation assignment for Lanternfall: two clips, one made from a sprite sheet and one that moves a rig. One loops, one commits. One authority drives them both. And four ideas to explain, each at a line of Bao's own clip, test or brief. Here's the ask, rebuilt from Bao's change brief.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about Lanternfall, a lamp-headed courier surviving three minutes in a fog-bound night market, into two Godot 4 animations: a two-frame walk cycle sliced from my own sprite sheet, and a cutout-rig dash unlocked by a level-up card, with startup, active and recovery frames. Pin what the courier shows today before you change anything, and give every clip a read-back test.

One clip that moves a rig: a dash, cut from one of those cells into head, arm, coat and legs. The walk loops; the dash commits, with startup, active and recovery. One authority drives both. And four ideas Bao has to explain: what a clip is, one authority, two clocks, and feel designed in frames.

beats.narration_text: Bao's brief, rewritten in Bao's own words, sets the dash down in frames at sixty a second. Startup, four frames: the courier dips and leans back, direction locked. Active, ten frames: fifty-five pixels at three hundred thirty a second. Recovery, six frames, still locked. Then a one-second cooldown. It's not invincible: each phase has its own rule for a hit. And the predicted failures, each with the check that would catch it: the body blending into dark ground, a gap between coat and legs, a hesitation at the loop, and cast frames mistaken for loop errors.

beats.narration_text: A clip is a list of keys, not a movie. This is the walk's frame track, in the clip resource. The path line names a node and a property: Body, frame. The times are zero and eight sixtieths of a second; the values, cells two and three. Update one means discrete: hold each value until the next key. And if the path named a property that didn't exist? Nothing would complain. The track would just do nothing.

beats.narration_text: Feel is designed in frames. The builder carries Bao's phase table: four, ten, six, at sixty a second. Every track has a key at each phase boundary: zero, four, fourteen and twenty. The spacing follows the phase: transition two through startup, an ease-in that accelerates into the push; one, linear, while active; point five through recovery, settling. When play says the timing is wrong, the table changes, and the keys follow.

beats.role_note: Code beat (code-then-result-v1): godot/features/player/player.gd lines 209-218 at 5f09b7f, read verbatim; the next beat shows the result.
beats.narration_text: One authority. This function is the only code that plays or seeks the courier's Animation Player. It asks the state machine for a clip and a time, both from integer tick counters: the walk ticks, or the dash ticks over sixty. Then play, and seek. The player is in manual mode, so it never advances on a clock of its own. The clip moves only when the sixty-hertz simulation ticks, which is the same tick gameplay reads the dash on.

beats.narration_text: Not invincible. A hit lands in every phase. Then the match on the dash phase applies Bao's rules: in startup, the dash is cancelled and no cooldown starts, because no dash happened. In recovery, the rest is cut, and the cooldown starts. An active dash carries on, damage and all.

props.title: Not invincible.
props.source: godot/features/player/player.gd · lines 233–240 · source revision 5f09b7f · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
# Not invincible: the hit lands in every phase. It cancels startup (no dash happened, so no cooldown) and the
	# rest of recovery (the cooldown starts); an active dash carries on.
	match dash_phase:
		"startup":
			_set_dash_phase("")
			dash_ticks = 0
		"recovery":
			_end_dash()

beats.narration_text: The read-back. This check walks every track of every clip and resolves it: first the node, then the property, or a bone for a 3D transform track, or a blend shape. The last branch is the one that matters here: a property name that isn't on the node gets reported, instead of failing in silence. It proves a track points at something real, not that it points at the right thing.

beats.role_note: Result of B14. Recorded tool output: evidence/courier_clips.json, evidence/assignment-7/mutations/mutations-required.json, evidence/assignment-7/godot3-names/probe.json.
beats.narration_text: Recorded output: eighty-six of eighty-six read-back checks. Then the assignment's four mutations, each in its own git worktree. Rename the rotation property, and track problems reports it. Switch the walk's loop off, and the loop check fails. Key cell ten on a ten-cell sheet, and three checks fail. Reimport from an empty cache, and everything still passes, because a cutout rig has no importer setting to lose. One surprise: in Godot four point seven, a Godot three style loop equals true still loops; only the name scan catches it. What no headless run can show is whether the motion reads.

beats.role_note: Recap of the four ideas; the excerpt is the first sentence of Bao's answer 5 in the brief, verbatim.
beats.narration_text: So, the four ideas, each at a line. What a clip is: keys on a node and a property, and a missing property fails silently unless the read-back resolves it. What one authority means: only the show function plays and seeks; a second writer would win by node order, not by design. What the two clocks are: the clip is seeked on the same sixty-hertz tick gameplay reads, measured zero seconds apart. And what feel in frames means: Bao's table, four, ten, six, became keys at zero, four, fourteen and twenty.
